fixes.explanation: Olives are a fair guess, but the king never says a word about them. His plan is the vineyard “…to use as a vegetable garden…” He also points out that it's right next to his palace. A king with a whole palace, servants, the works, and he wants to grow his own vegetables? You know that guy has one sad little tomato plant, and he checks on it every morning like it's a newborn baby.

Silver it is, baker. Ahab gives Naboth two choices: a better vineyard in its place, or if Naboth prefers, the vineyard's value in silver. Naboth is the vineyard's owner, and he answers, “The LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers.” Silver, a better vineyard, take your pick, and the man still says no. A king standing at your door with a blank check, and you just say no! I can't even say no to a second helping of my own dough.

problems.problem: The closing line still lacks a clear laugh. Being king doesn't make the lettuce-and-salad comparison click.
The 25-cent comparison is still flat and doesn't deliver a comic payoff.
